name: figma-outline-text-title-card
story: A designer drew a full-frame opening card with a show title and an episode line, then exported the frame as SVG with the 'Outline text' checkbox left ON, so both text layers arrived as vector.
idioms: no <?xml?> prolog, zero indentation, fill="none" on the root - the same Figma shell as the live-text export
not one <text> element anywhere in the file
Figma flattens an ENTIRE text layer into a single compound <path>, one 'd' whose subpaths are the glyphs - it does not emit a <g> of per-glyph paths
the outlined path keeps the text layer's name as its id (id="Show Title", id="Episode Number")
the original text fill survives on the path (fill="white", fill="#B7BCC4")
absolute path data with H/V shorthand and Figma's decimal habit
frame contents still inside <g clip-path="url(#clip0_31_204)"> with the matching <defs><clipPath>
whyThisMatters: Outlined text is the most common real-world SVG import failure, and this file breaks the stated recovery rule head-on: the docs offer an outline row for 'a group of two or more path/polygon shapes', while Figma hands over exactly one path per text layer - so a designer who names their layers 'Show Title' and 'Episode Number' should still be offered two recoverable rows plus a message naming the Outline-text checkbox, not a silent import with nothing editable.
